title: OpenAI Reassigns Quarter of Production Engineering Staff to Security Initiative
summary:
A manager known as 'General Tibo' has been appointed to lead a new internal security push at OpenAI, involving the reallocation of 25% of the company's production engineers to strengthen its infrastructure. The personnel shift focuses on hardening the AI lab's systems as its leadership believes the value of model weights will eventually exceed any possible security spending.

The initiative includes a security sprint with Cathedral Systems, a cybersecurity startup that previously penetrated internal HR and IT tools at competitor Anthropic in less than 12 hours. Alongside the partnership, OpenAI has increased the ceiling of its bug bounty program to pay as much as $300,000 per report, with rewards for critical vulnerabilities reaching $172,000 and prompt injection findings paying up to $130,000.

selectedTweets.text:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.
